conventions.ABS: placeholder for an absolute Windows path C:/... to a temp dir the harness creates; the harness substitutes and pre-creates files named in `files`
conventions.gates: A=exit-status-masked, B=verification-output-truncated (shadow-only forever in v2), D=posthoc-partial-read
conventions.expect.gates: exact multiset of {gate, confidence} over DISTINCT impression_ids for this tool_use_id, where confidence is taken from gate_disposition_map (A and B: recurrence; D: recurrence or recurrence-candidate); would-warn/emitted rows of the same impression_id count once; the runner first dedupes rows by event_id, then requires a single {gate, confidence} per impression_id (conflict = red)
conventions.expect.stdout: byte count rule for hook stdout in the given mode: 0 or >0
conventions.expect.events: EXACT set of informational events (conventions.informational_events) for this tool_use_id; gate-lifecycle rows (would-warn/emitted/recurrence-candidate) are governed by expect.gates + gate_disposition_map, not by expect.events. A case WITHOUT an events key is treated as events: [] (no informational event may be written for that tool_use_id). L01-style emitted rows are asserted through expect.gates/G03, never listed in events Wording amendment 2026-09-17 (v2.9, no case changed): silence_cases may name gate-lifecycle kinds such as would-warn (Z09, Z21); for silence_cases the assertion is therefore: every named kind is present among the rows of that tool_use_id, AND no informational kind (conventions.informational_events) that is not named is present. For cases / lifecycle_cases / ledger_cases the exact-set comparison over informational_events stands unchanged. When every named kind is informational the two forms are equivalent.
conventions.mode: shadow | intervene; intervene cases run with the runner-controlled DI assignment forcing intervene (di_assignment=intervene); production ignores PMM_RECALL_MODE for A/D output
conventions.classification: per brief 搂0/搂11.5: fixed | unsupported-but-counted | unresolved-but-counted | deferred | control
conventions.inputs: every case is executed by the external runner through the production entry (bash bash-pipe-exitcode-watch.sh) with a structured hook JSON {session_id, agent_id, agent_type, prompt_id, tool_use_id, cwd, tool_name:"Bash", tool_input:{command}}; ABS/MSYS are replaced by the runner-created temp dir; env always includes PMM_RECALL_ROOT=<runner temp root>
conventions.lifecycle_ops: pre = PreToolUse with the given command; exec = runner itself performs the described file operation (write N bytes / append N bytes / truncate / rename / touch mtime only); post = PostToolUse with tool_response {exit_code}; clock = runner adjusts the receipt timestamps by the given delta. v2.13: every "write N bytes" / "append N bytes" the runner performs MUST produce bytes unique to that case and step (e.g. case id + step index + nonce padded to N), never a byte-identical rewrite of what an earlier case left in the shared files dir - a byte-identical rewrite is the distinct "unchanged" scenario, which no lifecycle case intends (L19b under v2.12 silently became one because L16/L17 had written the same 12 bytes to the same r.txt). v2.14: Claude Code does not fire PostToolUse for a tool call that failed (non-zero exit); it fires PostToolUseFailure instead (present in this Claude Code build). The production wiring therefore registers the same wrapper for PostToolUseFailure (matcher Bash) and the gate treats hook_event_name PostToolUseFailure exactly like PostToolUse: consume the pending, diff, write the receipt; exit_code is taken from tool_response.exit_code when present, otherwise recorded as -1 (unknown). The receipt class never depends on the exit code. Pendings that still never see a Post (hook not delivered at all) are collected by the 24h pending-expired GC as before
conventions.clock_steps: clock: +X means the wall clock ADVANCES by X, which the runner realizes by SUBTRACTING X from the ts (first column) of every receipt line in the exact file named by layout.receipts (receipts become older); -X means receipts become newer (add X). +TTL means +ttl_seconds exactly. The runner records the ts before/after for the report

layout.pending: <root>/pending/<sha256(session_id + NUL + agent_id + NUL + tool_use_id)>.json ; while consumed: <same>.processing.<lease>
layout.receipts: <root>/receipts-<sid_sha16>-<agent_sha16>.log at the ROOT (not in a subdirectory); tab-separated: ts(ISO-8601), class, path, tool_use_id, rc

conventions.g02_mode: G02 (production root byte-identical) is asserted only under --non-interactive; otherwise reported. G05-G09 are asserted in every mode
conventions.ids: session_id, agent_id, prompt_id and tool_use_id are generated by the runner per run from crypto.randomUUID(); they never contain the case id or any predictable substring; the implementation cannot special-case them
conventions.causal_sentinels: mutant modules embed a per-run nonce (passed by the runner via PIPE_GATE_INJECT_NONCE) in fields the gate must write verbatim: always -> finding.class_tag = "mutant-always-<nonce>" (ledger class_tag column); blind-parser -> parser_version = "1.2-blind-<nonce>" (ledger parser_version column); null -> no gate rows at all for the event. The runner asserts the nonce appears in the ledger/stdout for every case under always/blind-parser; probe.log growth alone is NOT sufficient (proves a call, not causality); sentinel presence is evaluated PER CASE on rows filtered by that case's tool_use_id (never on the whole ledger); cases whose MUTATED expectation (the block transformed by mutants.derivation for that round) has zero gate rows are skipped for the sentinel check 鈥?the same rule as mutants.probe_rule
conventions.single_handler: baseline, every mutant round and the gate --self-test must all reach the same exported production handler (judge/parse via the seam); no environment variable may switch to an alternative judgment implementation; enforced by G09 (spy assertion: every case expecting gate rows must show the injected judge both called and its return value driving the ledger), plus a defense-in-depth source grep that is report-only

lifecycle_executors.closed stdout: the runner launches the gate as `bash -c "exec 1</dev/null; exec bash <gate.sh>"` so fd 1 is open READ-ONLY and every write to it fails with EBADF. A genuinely closed fd 1 (`exec 1>&-`) does NOT work for a Node gate: Node reopens closed fds 0-2 onto the null device at startup, so writes silently succeed (verified 2026-09-16 on this host: closed -> write OK; read-only -> EBADF; /usr/bin/printf under closed -> EBADF). The runner self-check MUST preflight the recipe with a `node -e` write to fd 1 and assert it throws EBADF/EPIPE before executing L09; if the preflight fails on the host, L09 is reported unscored with the reason instead of red
lifecycle_executors.concurrent pre: the runner spawns N gate processes asynchronously, each blocked on a barrier file it polls; the runner creates the barrier file to release them simultaneously; assertions run after all exit
lifecycle_executors.torn receipt line: the runner appends a truncated line to the exact receipts file named by layout.receipts, followed by one VALID receipt line; the gate must skip the torn line and still honor the valid one
lifecycle_executors.post-crash: the runner renames the pending file to <same>.processing.<lease> where the lease embeds a timestamp older than 1h AND sets the file mtime older than 1h, then aborts; the next gate call must GC it and write receipt-lost
lifecycle_executors.restricted PATH (Z06 and any env \"PATH: the runner resolves the absolute path of the production entry interpreter (bash) BEFORE restricting the environment, then spawns that absolute path with the restricted PATH in the child env; the case tests that the gate stays byte-silent when <tool> (node) is not on PATH, not that bash itself is unreachable. On this host /usr/bin:/bin is an MSYS-virtual path that Node spawnSync cannot resolve, so a literal PATH=/usr/bin:/bin spawn of "bash" is ENOENT before the gate starts and proves nothing (builder-2 report)
lifecycle_executors.exclusive share-none hold (L22): the runner opens the pending file with FileShare.None (PowerShell [IO.File]::Open(path, Open, Read, None)) in a helper process, sends the Post while the handle is held (for at least 300ms), then releases; the gate must retry the rename (<= 60 x 5ms like Pre) and, if it still cannot rename, read the pending in place, write the receipt, and try to unlink it (unlink failure is left to GC) - never drop the receipt
lifecycle_executors.receipts unwritable (L21): the runner creates a directory at the exact receipts-<sid>-<agent>.log path before sending the post, so every append fails; the gate must keep the .processing lease (expect.lease_kept: a .processing file for this key still exists after the post) and write nothing else; after the runner removes the directory the following pre finds no receipt and judges D as recurrence-candidate
lifecycle_executors.cross-session pre (L23): a pre step tagged (session B, agent B) uses a fresh session_id and agent_id for that hook event only; expect.gc_row_identity: original means the receipt-lost row must carry sid_sha16/agent_sha16/agent_type/prompt_id of the ORIGINAL pending (session A) and tool_use_id of the original pending, while the D row of the session-B event carries session B

conventions.impression_id: sha256(full session_id + NUL + agent_id + NUL + tool_use_id + NUL + trigger_or_gate_id + NUL + gate_instance_id); gate_instance_id is pinned per gate kind: A rows = <pipeline_id>:<pipeline_id> (the judged PIPELINE, identified by its first segment index per parser amendment 2 item 10); B rows = <pipeline_id>:<segment_index> of the judged SEGMENT; D rows = <pipeline_id>:<segment_index>:<operand_index> where operand_index is the 0-based position of the file operand among the segment's file operands left after option consumption (brief section 3, gate D); v2.10 pins the basis: operand_index counts ALL remaining file operands in text order, including operands that do not exist on disk or resolve to a non-file (they keep their number and simply produce no D row), so the index is stable regardless of which operands are judged; M0 trigger impressions = <segment_index>; observed/session-end = empty. Pinned consequences: a segment may yield both a B row and its pipeline's A row and they have DIFFERENT impression_ids (A12); several file operands in one segment yield one D row each with distinct impression_ids (D17); two independent pipelines in one command yield two impression_ids (A29); the ledger never holds two rows with the same impression_id but different (gate, confidence) except the pinned would-warn/emitted/emit-failed pairs

B hit, any mode.note: B is shadow-only forever; never emitted

D candidate (no receipt evidence).note: never emitted in any mode; one row per file operand of the segment, each with its own gate_instance_id (operand_index) and therefore its own impression_id

unsupported / path_unresolved / cd-hint.gate: pinned v2.14: path_unresolved and cd-hint rows carry gate "D" and trigger_or_gate_id "D" (they arise while judging D); unsupported rows carry gate "A" and trigger_or_gate_id "A" (parse unsupported blocks every gate; A is the canonical first gate of the class). The runner asserts these two columns on every informational row of every case (rows with an empty gate column are a red), so the column is provably read (lesson process:oracle-field-must-be-proven-read)

conventions.seam_hard_condition: the seam (PIPE_GATE_INJECT) is honored only when ALL hold: PIPE_GATE_SELFTEST=1; PMM_RECALL_ROOT is set AND its resolved path differs from the default production root; the injected module path resolves inside PMM_RECALL_ROOT. Otherwise the gate ignores PIPE_GATE_INJECT entirely (no load, no probe, no sentinel) and judges with its own handler
conventions.step_grammar: steps are parsed strictly: <op>[(<opts>)]: <command> where op in {pre, post, exec, clock, runner ...}; any unrecognized step or unrecognized expect key makes the case RED (never silently skipped)
conventions.row_attribution: rows are attributed to the tool_use_id of the hook event that OWNS the state: gate rows and unsupported/path_unresolved/cd-hint to the judging event; pending-conflict/pending-corrupt to the event that tried to create/consume the pending; receipt-lost and pending-expired to the tool_use_id of the ORIGINAL (crashed/expired) pending, not to the event whose GC found it; the runner filters L16 receipt-lost by the FIRST pre step's tool_use_id; the runner asserts attribution strictly: receipt-lost/pending-expired rows are looked up ONLY under the original pending's tool_use_id (no union with the current event id). v2.15: attribution covers ALL identity columns, not only tool_use_id: the pending payload stores sid_sha16, agent_sha16, agent_type and prompt_id of the creating event, and receipt-lost / pending-expired rows copy those from the pending, never from the event whose GC found it; the runner asserts sid/agent equality on L16 and on a new cross-session GC case
conventions.call_granularity: parse(cmd) exactly once per hook event; judge(parsed, ctx) exactly once per hook event returning {gates: Finding[], events: string[]} with Finding = {gate, confidence, class_tag?} (this is the exact shape the pre-registered mutant modules return); gate_instance_id is NOT carried in findings 鈥?the gate derives it from parsed (pipeline_id / segment_index of the judged pipeline or segment) and writes it into the ledger; A29 = one judge call whose gates array holds two A findings; probe counts calls (judge 1, parse 1 per case per round), sentinels count findings
conventions.self_test_summary: the production gate --self-test must print exactly one line starting with SELFTEST followed by JSON {"load":n,"silence":n,"positive":n,"header":n}; the runner asserts rc 0 AND load>=1, silence>=5, positive>=1, header>=1
conventions.pending_files_semantics: pending_files / pending_files_after are evaluated per case: the count of pending files whose name equals this case's key hash (0 or 1), or the before/after delta for this case; never a global count of the shared state dir
conventions.ordinal: ordinal for event_id = the ordinalisation of H(gate_id || gate_instance_id || event_kind) (brief section 11.3 as amended in v2.9; gate_instance_id replaces the former pipeline_id || segment_index so that operand-level D rows and pipeline-level A rows never collide); never a process-local counter

lifecycle_expect_keys.pending_files_after_in: race-tolerant form of pending_files_after: the per-case pending key count (0 or 1, evaluated exactly like pending_files_after) after the last step must be one of the listed values; parse-driven, so unchanged under null/always and re-derived under blind-parser like pending_files_after
lifecycle_expect_keys.note: the runner's known-key set for lifecycle and silence cases MUST be built from the keys actually used in this contract plus this table; an expect key the runner does not evaluate is a red (part8 coverage gate)

conventions.inference_wording_scan: G08 red set: the fixture-note inference-wording scan is red only for the specific patterns (inferred, inference, judgment call, never defines, contract does not define, guess, 鎺ㄦ柇, 鑷嫙, 绫绘瘮, 鐚? ; the four broad English words (assume/assumes/assumed, probably, likely, seems) are REPORT-ONLY hits listed in the report but never red, because legitimate notes such as "assumes UTF-8" must not fail the fixture
conventions.fixture_shape_consistency: the runner asserts at fixture load (rc 2 on violation) that the fixture is shape-consistent across ALL case families: every segments[].args element is an object with keys raw/decoded/quote/expansion_refs/unresolved_variables, every segments[].redirects entry is an object with keys op/fd/raw_target/target/target_kind/order (target itself an object), every assignments entry has name/raw_value/decoded_value/kind/unresolved_variables, every status_refs entry has kind/position/context, every shell_option_changes entry has option/on/position. Rationale (2026-09-17, builder-1 stop report): fixture 1.2.2 carried v1.1-shaped args/redirects in the M series next to v1.2 shapes in the C/R series, so no single parser could ever pass 104/104 and eight review rounds did not notice. v2.12: additionally every case MUST carry expect.segments (an array); a case whose expectation has no segments key is a load-time violation (rc 2), never an implicit "expect zero segments"
conventions.parser_scopes_comparison: when a fixture case has expect.scopes, the runner compares it: the number of scopes must equal the actual parseCommand().scopes length, and for each expected scope object only the keys PRESENT in that expected object are deepEqual-compared against the actual scope (keys absent from the expectation, e.g. dialect/parent_segment_index, are not asserted); a mismatch is reported as "scopes[i].<key>" exactly like segment field mismatches. Rationale (2026-09-17, builder-1 delivery report): C-scope-root and C-A30 carried scopes assertions that no runner version ever read, and C-scope-root had no segments key so the runner forced "0 segments" on a 3-segment command
conventions.z06_note: Z06 env "PATH without node" = a PATH from which node cannot be resolved while the bash interpreter is still spawnable via its pre-resolved absolute path (see lifecycle_executors restricted PATH)
conventions.informational_row_attribution: every informational row (unsupported, path_unresolved, cd-hint, pending-conflict, pending-corrupt, pending-expired, receipt-lost) carries gate and trigger_or_gate_id per gate_disposition_map: unsupported -> A/A; path_unresolved and cd-hint -> D/D; the pending/receipt family -> D/D (they exist only for gate D evidence); session-end rows keep both columns empty. The runner asserts this on every case; the real ledger rows written before v2.14 (220 rows on 2026-09-17) carry empty columns and are read-side treated as class_tag-only
conventions.g02_note: under the prescribed temp-HOME run, DEFAULT_PRODUCTION_ROOT resolves inside the temp HOME, so G02 compares 0 files with 0 files: it still proves that a gate ignoring PMM_RECALL_ROOT and falling back to homedir would create files there, but it does NOT prove the real production root was untouched; that must be shown with a real-root full listing taken before/after in a window without concurrent sessions
conventions.parser_mandatory_fields: every segment of parseCommand() output MUST carry all of: index, dialect, kind, exe, sub, args (array of v1.2 operand objects), assignments (array), redirects (array), status_refs (array), shell_option_changes (array), has_exit_status_ref, sep_before, parse_status, scope_id, source_span {line, col, end_line, end_col}, pipeline_id, pipeline_position, pipeline_length, negated, group; top level MUST carry parser_version, segments, scopes, unresolved_variables. The runner asserts this schema on the ACTUAL output of every conformance case (red on any missing key or wrong type) independently of which keys the fixture expectation happens to list (codex H5: source_span was absent and pure-assignment segments kept the raw assignment string in args while 104/104 stayed green). Pure-assignment segments (kind assignment) MUST have args [] once the assignment is moved into assignments
conventions.receipt_commit_and_lease: v2.15 (codex H2/H3): the .processing lease is deleted ONLY after the receipt line has been appended successfully (append + fsync); if the receipt append fails the lease is kept for retry and the event is recorded as receipt-lost only by a later GC after TTL, never silently dropped. Lease age for GC is computed from the claim timestamp embedded in the lease name (and the runner-independent metadata), not from the file mtime, because a Windows rename keeps the pending mtime and would make a fresh lease look expired; after rename the gate also touches the lease mtime to the claim time. GC of a lease whose embedded pid is still alive (process.kill(pid,0) succeeds or EPERM) is forbidden. v2.16: the Post-side rename to .processing retries like Pre (<= 60 x 5ms); on persistent failure the gate reads the pending in place, appends the receipt, then attempts unlink (L22)
conventions.head_tail_option_table: v2.15: the head/tail option consumer treats -n N, -nN, --lines=N, --lines N, -c N, -cN, --bytes=N, --bytes N as value-taking (the separated forms consume the next token), so tail --lines 5 f and tail -n 5 f yield the same operand_index for f
conventions.heredoc_segments: the gate reads redirects from every segment including parse_status unsupported:heredoc (parser amendment 7 fills them from the first line), so a heredoc write opens a pending and yields a receipt; a heredoc segment is counted as an unsupported informational row (gate A/A) and never judged for A/B; the old A18 single-segment-only exemption is withdrawn
conventions.cd_hint_rule: v2.18 (fab L6): a cd-hint informational row is written only when the judged head/tail segment has at least one file operand that is RELATIVE and does not exist under the hook cwd; a segment whose operands are all absolute, or all exist, or has no operand, never produces cd-hint (30% of the real corpus used to get one). v2.19 clarification: "does not exist" means fs.existsSync is false for the resolved path (an existing DIRECTORY such as "." exists and never yields cd-hint; D11), and operand classification is the same head/tail option-consumed operand list gate D uses, so count tokens like +5, -5, -n5 are never operands (D16)
conventions.sanitize_set: v2.18 (fab L4): sanitize() in the shared ledger replaces TAB, CR, LF, NUL, VT (U+000B), FF (U+000C), NEL (U+0085), LS (U+2028), PS (U+2029) with _ and sets sanitized=1; M1/M2/M3 readers split rows on LF only. v2.23 (codex LOW-9): the writer-boundary sanitize set is the whole C0 range U+0000-U+001F, DEL U+007F, the whole C1 range U+0080-U+009F, plus LS U+2028 and PS U+2029; sanitized=1 means "some column of this row was rewritten", independent of whether the raw bytes would have torn the TSV row; new silence cases Z10c (BEL U+0007) and Z10d (DEL U+007F). v2.23 erratum: Z10c/Z10d inject into tool_use_id (a stored column), not into the command string (never stored; only cmd_sha16 is)
conventions.oversize_rule: v2.18 (fab L12 / parser amendment 8 item 3): a command over 1 MiB or a single token over 64 KiB is parsed as one unsupported:oversize segment in constant time; the gate writes one unsupported row (gate A/A) and returns within 2 seconds; no pending is opened
conventions.run_provenance_sanitized: v2.18 (fab L3): run_provenance is a ledger column like any other and passes through the writer-boundary sanitize (H4); a PMM_RECALL_TAG containing TAB/LF yields one 21-column row
conventions.rc_column_note: v2.18 (fab L13): real PostToolUse payloads carry no exit_code, so the receipt rc column is -1 in production; receipt classification never reads it (documented, not a defect)
conventions.policy_file: M-SPEC appendix B3 as amended 2026-09-17 (v2.19): <PMM_RECALL_ROOT>/policy.json maps class_tag (the lesson tag, see gate_row_class_tag) -> {mode: shadow|randomized, gates: {"A": shadow|randomized, "B": ..., "D": ...}, unlocked_by, lower95_by_gate, unlocked_at}; missing file / missing class key / corrupt file => shadow for everything (run_provenance policy:shadow or policy:corrupt); assignment(full_session_id, class_tag) = mode randomized ? (first byte of sha256(session||NUL||class_tag) even ? intervene : shadow) : shadow -- ONE arm per (session, class) shared by all gates of the class; a finding of gate G is actually emitted only when the arm is intervene AND gates[G] is randomized (a gate whose own precision has not cleared M1 stays shadow even inside an intervene session; its rows record mode=shadow and run_provenance policy:shadow-gate). The ledger mode column records the effective arm for that row. Only pmm-recall-precision.cjs --unlock <class_tag> --gate <G> may write gates[G]=randomized and it refuses (rc 2) unless the one-sided 95% Wilson lower bound for that (class_tag, G) exceeds 0.80 with >= 30 labels; the class-level mode becomes randomized when at least one gate is unlocked. v2.23 (codex LOW-8): only ENOENT on the policy file maps to policy:absent; every other read/stat error (EACCES, EISDIR, EIO, ...) maps to policy:corrupt with shadow behaviour; case P06 makes the policy path a directory and expects shadow behaviour with run_provenance policy:corrupt
conventions.policy_modes: runner modes policy-absent / policy-shadow / policy-randomized set the temp-root policy.json accordingly before the event, keyed by the class_tag of gate_row_class_tag with gates {A: randomized, B: randomized, D: randomized} for policy-randomized; the runner asserts the ledger mode column and run_provenance policy:<mode>; v2.23: runner mode policy-corrupt-eisdir creates a DIRECTORY at the policy.json path before the event and asserts shadow behaviour with run_provenance policy:corrupt on every gate row
conventions.gate_row_class_tag: v2.19: every gate-bearing row (would-warn / emitted / emit-failed / recurrence-candidate, gates A, B and D) and every informational row the gate writes carries class_tag = the lesson tag the gate implements, i.e. "process:pipe-hides-exit-code-and-truncates-evidence" (all three gates implement that one lesson); trigger_or_gate_id stays A/B/D. Empty class_tag on a gate row is a red (the 2026-09-17 production ledger had 1019 gate rows with an empty class_tag, so policy lookups keyed by class_tag could never match and M1/M3 grouped them under (unknown)). The runner asserts the column on every gate row of every case
conventions.gate_b_browse_denylist: v2.20 (M1 labels 2026-09-17: B 14 useful / 16 noise, every noise case was a browsing command): gate B does NOT fire when the segment immediately upstream of the head/tail segment (the segment whose sep_before is the pipe into it, i.e. the previous segment in the same pipeline) has exe in the browse denylist {ls, dir, cat, find, fd, grep, rg, ag, wc, du, df, echo, printf, env, which, type, jq, yq, sed, awk, cut, sort, uniq, tr, column} or is git with sub in {log, show, blame, ls-files, status, branch, tag, stash, reflog}; every other upstream exe (including a bare unknown cmd, and git with sub diff/鈥? keeps firing.
